### 1) What is on the screen
One frame of a black story card. Top ~55% is near-solid black with ~20 single-pixel white star dots. Bottom ~35% is six lines of centered white all-caps pixel text on black. The eye goes first to the middle white line WEARS THIN. in region 253,538,262,36. The player is being asked to read lore - THEY WERE FORGOTTEN / AND THE VEIL BETWEEN / THEIR WORLD AND OURS / WEARS THIN. / TODAY A SCIENTIST, A STUDENT, / A SAILOR AND A CEO. I cannot see any player, enemies, HUD, map, or press prompt - I cannot see what game this is or what input comes next.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES - FAIL. Impression is 2 colours, black+white, but measured facts overrule: 215 distinct colours in file vs hardware ceiling 25 colours, and 210 colour(s) NOT in the 64 entry NES palette. This file is OVER the ceiling.
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape, no gradient banding - PASS. No gradients, no pillow shading visible; 92.4% of frame is one black; shapes are flat.
(c) sprites read at a glance against background - FAIL. I cannot see any sprites. Only background text in region 10,424,748,226 and 1-pixel stars in region 0,20,768,380. No OAM silhouette to read, no 8x8 / 8x16 separation.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges anywhere - FAIL. Impression is crisp, but measurement proves filtering: 210 non-NES colours are almost always anti-aliasing. At 768x720, exactly 3x 256x240, a clean integer scale would still be 2 colours. The gray fringe around white glyphs is soft edges, forbidden - real NES has no alpha, no anti-aliasing.
(e) colour changes in background land on the 16x16 grid - PASS. Only backdrop black + white text tiles visible, no drifting attribute zones. Stars are single pixels inside tiles, which does not by itself break the 16x16 palette boundary rule for backgrounds.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded: text block 10,424,748,226 packs six lines edge-to-edge with no window, no margin. Empty: star void 0,0,768,400 is 92.4% empty black with sparse random dots, no horizon, no structure. Focal point - central text 253,538,262,36 - is where the player needs it for a story card, but with no PRESS START cue the eye dies at the bottom. All text is high-contrast white on black and legible at 256x240 in principle. Rows: Row1 138,424,492,36 THEY WERE FORGOTTEN, / Row2 138,462,492,36 AND THE VEIL BETWEEN / Row3 135,500,498,36 THEIR WORLD AND OURS / Row4 253,538,262,36 WEARS THIN. / Row5 10,576,748,36 TODAY A SCIENTIST, A STUDENT, / Row6 108,614,552,36 A SAILOR AND A CEO. Worst is Row5 10,576,748,36: it runs 10,576 to 758,612, touching overscan with ~10 file pixels (~3 NES pixels) margin; commas crowd, line will clip on CRT and has no breathing room unlike the centered rows above.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
Honest layout, dishonest export. No gibberish text, no pillow shading, no melted glyphs - this reads as a handmade cutscene card, not a prompt render. What is off is technical:
- filtered upscale: 210 colours outside NES 64-entry palette as gray halos on text, not whole NES $0F black / $30 white tiles.
- text not on clean glyph grid: stems show 3-4 gray steps instead of hard 3x3 blocks for one NES pixel.
- borders not a whole number of tiles: no window frame at all, text floats on backdrop with no 8-pixel tile discipline.
- stray pixels: random 1-pixel stars in 0,20,768,380 with no 8x8 tile repetition, uneven density, one cross-shaped artifact near 240,285,12,12.
- empty-prompt composition: 92.4% one colour with no direction, reads as placeholder export, not shipped staging.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Crush palette in region 0,0,768,720: map every pixel to only NES $0F Black #000000 and NES $30 White #FFFFFF with nearest-neighbor threshold, delete other 213 colours to meet 25 colours on screen, 4 background palettes limit.
2. Redraw worst row in region 10,576,748,36 TODAY A SCIENTIST, A STUDENT,: redraw at native 256x240 in 8x8 font, then 3x nearest-neighbor with no filter, and shrink / re-track to leave 24 file pixels = 8 NES pixels side margin; move row 24 pixels left to region 10,576,724,36 to clear overscan.
3. Fix stars in region 0,20,768,380: erase all current 1-pixel noise, re-place 12 stars as 6x6 file pixel = 2x2 NES pixel solid NES $30 White squares snapped to 8-pixel multiples, e.g. at 48,48 and 192,96, no gray.
4. Move whole text block from region 10,424,748,226 up by 48 file pixels = 16 NES pixels = one attribute row to region 10,376,748,226 to balance empty top vs crowded bottom and free space for prompt.
5. Add advance cue in region 300,660,168,30: add PRESS START in NES $30 White on NES $0F Black, 8x8 tiles, one tile high, centered, blinking every 30 frames; I cannot see any cue now.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
nes_authenticity: 2/10 - 2-colour look but 215 colours, 210 non-NES, filtered edges.
readability: 8/10 - white on black caps readable, except Row5 edge clipping.
charm: 3/10 - stark void + flat text, no framing, no sprite acting.
